definition: The bank-assigned identifier that uniquely identifies a customer relationship across all products and systems. The anchor key for every aggregation performed on a customer.
The 13-digit national identity number of an individual customer, used as the primary external matching key and the basis of identity verification.
The tax registration number of a corporate or business customer, used for tax reporting and corporate entity matching.
Classification of the customer as individual, sole proprietor, partnership, private or public company, government or financial institution. Determines regulatory treatment and reporting bucket.
The money-laundering risk classification assigned to the customer, driving the intensity of due diligence and monitoring applied.
The date by which the customer's due diligence documentation must next be refreshed, derived from risk rating and last review date.
The natural person or persons who ultimately own or control a corporate customer, above the applicable ownership threshold.
The recorded relationship linking a customer to a wider group of connected entities for the purpose of aggregate exposure measurement.
Indicator that the customer, or a close associate, holds or has held prominent public function, triggering enhanced due diligence.
The country of residence and domicile of the customer, determining cross-border treatment, tax obligations and reporting classification.
The unique identifier of a deposit or current account arrangement, and the join key between core banking, GL and downstream reporting.
The current operational state of the account — active, dormant, blocked, closed, unclaimed — determining reporting treatment and permitted activity.
The book balance of the account at close of business, before uncleared effects. The primary input to deposit reporting and reserve computation.
The identifier of the product under which the arrangement was opened, determining pricing, regulatory bucket and reporting classification.
The denomination currency of the arrangement, driving revaluation, foreign-currency reporting and open-position measurement.
The date the arrangement came into effect, used for vintage analysis, dormancy computation and tenure-based reporting.
The contractual maturity date of a term deposit, driving the maturity ladder used in liquidity and repricing analysis.
The contracted rate applied to the deposit, including the profit rate for Islamic deposit products, driving cost of funds and FTP.
Flag segregating Islamic banking arrangements from conventional ones, required for separate books, returns and profit distribution.
The organisational unit at which the arrangement is booked, used for geographic reporting, branch profitability and regional aggregation.
Unique identifier of a credit facility or loan arrangement, the anchor for all exposure, classification and provisioning measurement.
The principal amount currently outstanding on the facility, exclusive of accrued markup. The base measure for exposure and provisioning.
The approved credit limit for the facility, used for undrawn commitment measurement and limit-utilisation monitoring.
The number of days since the earliest unpaid contractual obligation fell due. The primary driver of classification and staging.
The prudential classification of the facility — regular, OAEM, substandard, doubtful or loss — determining the minimum provisioning requirement.
The impairment stage (1, 2 or 3) assigned under the expected credit loss framework, determining whether 12-month or lifetime loss is recognised.
Indicator that the facility's terms have been modified due to borrower financial difficulty, with the associated classification consequences.
Modelled likelihood that the obligor defaults within the applicable horizon; a primary ECL and capital input.
Modelled proportion of exposure expected to be lost on default after recoveries, incorporating collateral realisation assumptions.
The expected exposure amount at the point of default, incorporating drawn balance and expected further drawdown of committed limits.
The contractual maturity of the credit facility, driving repricing, liquidity ladder placement and lifetime ECL horizon.
The contracted rate on the facility together with its benchmark and repricing frequency, driving interest income and rate-sensitivity analysis.
The sector of economic activity of the borrower, driving sectoral concentration reporting and risk-weighting in some treatments.
The specific and general provision carried against the facility, reconciling to the general ledger provisioning accounts.
Unique identifier of a security item pledged against one or more facilities.
The assessed realisable value of the security and the date of that assessment, determining eligibility for provisioning benefit.
consumers: Forced sale value benefit in provisioning

definition: The category of security held and whether it qualifies as eligible for regulatory credit risk mitigation.
The linkage and allocated proportion of a collateral item to each facility it secures, preventing double-counting of security benefit.
The tokenised reference identifying a payment card, linking card activity to the customer and account without exposing the card number itself.
Current outstanding balance and approved limit on a credit card account, feeding exposure, undrawn commitment and delinquency measurement.
The value and denomination of a financial transaction, the atomic input to monitoring, reconciliation and income recognition.
The classification of a transaction by nature and purpose, driving monitoring scenarios and statistical reporting of flows.
Identifying details of the other party to a transfer, required for screening, wire-transfer information rules and investigation.
The effective value date and the ledger posting date of a transaction, distinct fields whose conflation causes systematic reconciliation breaks.
The chart-of-accounts code against which a balance or movement is recorded, and the pivot of all financial and regulatory reporting.
The mapping from internal GL codes to the regulator's prescribed reporting chart of accounts. The single most examined mapping in the estate.
The closing balance per GL account per reporting period, which must reconcile to the sum of underlying subledger positions.
The organisational unit to which income and expense are attributed, driving segment reporting and internal profitability.
The rate applied to revalue foreign currency positions at reporting date, driving revaluation gains and open-position measurement.
Designation of an investment as held-to-maturity, available-for-sale or held-for-trading, determining valuation and P&L treatment.
Indicator of whether an asset qualifies toward the statutory liquidity requirement, determining reserve compliance computation.
The modelled maturity profile applied to non-maturity deposits and prepayable assets in liquidity and rate-risk analysis, replacing contractual terms.
The approved definition of a governed business term, its owner, approval date and status. Governance metadata is itself a critical data element.
The sensitivity classification assigned to a data element, driving masking, access control and permissibility of external processing.
The recorded Data Owner and Steward for each governed element. Without this, no other governance control has an accountable party.
The recorded source-to-consumption path for a governed element, including transformation logic at each hop.

The enterprise-assigned identifier that resolves a person or organisation to one record across every operational and analytical system. Every aggregation by counterparty is only as trustworthy as this key.
The registered legal name of the party as it appears on the constitutive document or identity credential, distinct from any trading or display name.
The classification that determines which rules apply to a party — individual or organisation, resident or non-resident, related party or not. Drives downstream segmentation and eligibility.
The email address, telephone number or messaging handle designated for a stated purpose. A contact point is only critical because a legally required notice must reach it.
The structured postal or registered address of a party, with its jurisdiction component separable — jurisdiction drives tax, privacy and regulatory treatment.
The identifier for a sellable or serviceable offering, stable across its lifecycle and across the systems that price, deliver and account for it.
The dates bounding the period in which a product version may be sold and serviced. Overlapping or open-ended versions make point-in-time restatement impossible.
The price or rate agreed with a counterparty for a product, including its effective date. The single most frequent source of billing dispute and revenue leakage.
The identifier for a member of the workforce, the join key between HR, access management and the ownership and stewardship registers.
The grant that permits an identity to read or change a given data set. Governance is unprovable without it: you cannot evidence a control over data you cannot say who can reach.
The identifier resolving a supplier to one record across procurement, accounts payable and third-party risk.
The start, end and notice dates of a contractual obligation. Missing renewal dates convert into auto-renewals nobody decided to accept.
The account code in the chart of accounts to which a posting is made, and its mapping to the statutory disclosure line.
The organisational unit a cost is attributed to, and its position in the current management hierarchy.
The record of a data subject permitting a stated processing purpose, with its timestamp, scope and withdrawal state. Processing without it is unlawful, not merely ungoverned.
The retention rule applying to a data set — how long it is kept, on what legal basis, and what happens at expiry. The control that makes deletion defensible and over-retention detectable.
The identifier for an individual business event, unique and stable across the systems that capture, enrich and account for it.
The monetary value of an event with its currency and, where converted, the rate and rate date. An amount without an explicit currency is the most common silent corruption in consolidated reporting.
A permitted value in a controlled list — country, currency, status, category — together with its version. Uncontrolled code sets are how the same concept acquires four spellings.
A unit in the management hierarchy with its parent, effective dates and manager. Reorganisations silently break every historical roll-up that assumed the hierarchy was static.
